brief.title: Midterm brief: Saturday, October 17
brief.markdown:
# Midterm brief: Saturday, October 17

## Bottom line
Forecasters rate the House as leaning Democratic; all 10 forecasters have more seats rated for Democrats ([Wikipedia ratings table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_election_ratings)). The Senate is closer: 46 D and 44 R seats are solid or likely, with 10 competitive ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_Senate_elections)). Markets price Democratic control at 90.5% for the House and 64.5% for the Senate ([Polymarket House](https://polymarket.com/event/which-party-will-win-the-house-in-2026), [Senate](https://polymarket.com/event/which-party-will-win-the-senate-in-2026)), as of Oct 17.

## What moved
- **Cook Political Report (Oct 16):** All 11 of its House changes moved toward Democrats. FL-25 moved from Tossup to Lean D, and MT-01 from Lean R to Tossup; MN-01, NY-21, OH-10, OH-15 and SC-01 moved from Likely R to Lean R. Cook's count went from 213 D / 201 R to 214 / 200 ([Wikipedia ratings table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_House_of_Representatives_election_ratings)).
- **Consensus changes:** MT-01 is now a Tossup, and OH-15 moved from Likely R to Lean R and is now tracked.

## Races to watch today
- **Texas, Kansas and Maine Senate (Tossups):** InsiderAdvantage polls ending Oct 14 show Paxton 49, Talarico 48; Marshall 48, Hamilton 47; and Jackson 49, Collins 47 ([InsiderAdvantage](https://insideradvantage.com/insideradvantage-senate-surveys-texas-paxton-49-talarico-48-kansas-marshall-48-hamilton-47-maine-jackson-49-collins-47/)). Averages: TX D+1.5, KS D+0.5, ME D+2.6.
- **Ohio Senate special (Tossup):** Bowling Green State/YouGov shows Brown +6, ending Oct 9 ([BGSU](https://scholarworks.bgsu.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1030&context=depo)); average D+2.9.
- **Minnesota Senate (Lean D):** Flanagan and Tafoya held their only debate ([Washington Post via Google News](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMirgFBVV95cUxOaXJaV0hNc2F5YWtPeHMweTZORXBLTFBsajdtbmxHSW1oZGlzVkRqWTdyWmZfeDltN1pqbXo5c0kzZ1MwdFg5MEVXU0NQOUR3MGcydHZEOE1Qb29ZNmtjbUJEUHkyekxtNkxzYlVEM0xGRlBrVjlDSm5QUjktNjlnbS1NRU0zRHBrQUV6X1RGczVLNGZTZ1ZJUmlFRzdwblA0OXFXa1IwR013LTVGSFE?oc=5)). Average: D+4.3.
- **Michigan Senate (Lean D):** Ocasio-Cortez moved $1 million to El-Sayed ([NYT](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/16/us/politics/aoc-el-sayed-million-transfer-midterms.html)). Average: D+3.3, down from D+3.9 after a Republican-sponsored Tyson Group poll.

## Early vote
These are ballots by party registration, not votes, and mail ballots have leaned Democratic since 2020.
- **North Carolina:** Through Oct 15, 237,541 ballots were cast, 125% of the 2022 total at the same point (189,375) ([NCSBE](https://s3.amazonaws.com/dl.ncsbe.gov/Press/2026%20General/NC%20Absentee%20Stats%20for%202026%20General/2026-10-16%20Daily%20Absentee%20Stats%20Report%20-%202026%20General.pdf)). By Oct 16 the total reached 437,214, at D 45.4% / R 20.6% / other 34.0% against an even registration split; the Republican share is rising as in-person voting grows ([NCSBE data file](https://dl.ncsbe.gov/?prefix=ENRS/2026_11_03/)).
- **Florida and Pennsylvania (Oct 16):** Florida has 816,890 mail ballots at D 42.5% / R 36.3%, against registration of D 30.1% / R 41.5%. Pennsylvania has 456,065 at D 68.7% / R 22.8% ([UF Election Lab](https://election.lab.ufl.edu/early-vote/2026-early-voting/), state data).
- **Senate battlegrounds (Oct 16):** Maine has 101,403 ballots at D 53.2% / R 19.4%; Iowa 33,417 at D 53.9% / R 30.0%; Arizona 165,881 at D 40.7% / R 37.1% (via a private compiler) ([UF Election Lab](https://election.lab.ufl.edu/early-vote/2026-early-voting/)).

## What the spectrum is saying
- **Left:** No new left-leaning episode today beyond yesterday's Pod Save America ([Pod Save America](https://audioboom.com/posts/8965578)).
- **Center-left:** NPR reports Trump promised a swing-district blitz but is mostly visiting deep-red states ([NPR](https://www.npr.org/2026/10/17/nx-s1-6004276/trump-travel-midterms)).
- **Center-right:** The Dispatch argues a midterm loss could be a blessing in disguise for Republicans ([The Dispatch](https://thedispatch.com/newsletter/boilingfrogs/midterms-trump-republicans-benefit-losing/)).
- **Right:** National Review asks whether "woke" politics is returning ([National Review](https://www.nationalreview.com/2026/10/is-it-the-return-of-woke/)). This is opinion, not reporting.

## Talking points
- The generic ballot averages D+6.3 across 3 polls; Pew has D+8, ending Oct 4 ([Pew](https://www.pewresearch.org/politics/2026/10/08/with-americans-in-a-sour-mood-democratic-voters-are-more-engaged-in-midterms)).

## Coverage note
All 24 sources reported, and early vote covered 22 states. Kalshi had no priced markets. FL-22, SC-01 and TX-35 candidate parties remain unresolved.
